name: Stormy Blue
lede: Stormy Blue is a muted, grey-leaning [[blue]] named for storm-cloud weather, close in our library to [[steel-blue|Steel Blue]].

sections.title: Weather, not a material
sections.body:
Our graph files this as a landscape word, recorded by the 2010 xkcd crowd survey [1]. The ISCC-NBS block for it reads "moderate blue", and in Munsell terms it sits near 1.6PB 4.9/5.7 [1].

Its nearest library neighbor is [[dull-blue|Dull Blue]], and [[denim|Denim]] sits close in the same grey-blue family [1]. The hex is a screen value; no pigment or dye is implied [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Stormy Blue covers at least 2% of the canvas in 173 of our 23,781 paintings, and by position in each painting's lightness order it is found in 94, more common than 58% of the named colors we track, as photographed [2]. It most often plays an accent, the role in 43% of those matched paintings [2].

It peaks in the 1920s, in 5 of 237 paintings, at 3.3 times the archive's baseline rate for that decade, and in the 1900s overall at 2.9 times [2]. The earliest match is 1445, in a work by Michele Giambono, 565 years before the name's own 2010 record, a resemblance in an aged photograph rather than evidence of the name or the mix, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
